title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 232 (Performance of contract with agent supposed to be principal)

content.overview: Section 232 provides that where one man makes a contract with another, neither knowing nor having reasonable ground to suspect that the other is an agent, the principal, if he requires the performance of the contract, can only obtain such performance subject to the rights and obligations subsisting between the agent and the other party to the contract. Illustration: A owes B ₹500 and, as agent for C unknown to B, sells rice to B — C cannot compel B to take the rice without allowing set-off of A’s debt.
content.glance: Undisclosed principal enforcing contract takes subject to equities between agent and third party.
content.study: Where a person contracts with another neither knowing nor having reasonable ground to suspect that the other is an agent, the principal who requires performance can obtain it only subject to the rights and obligations subsisting between the agent and the other party. Illustration: A, who owes ₹500 to B, sells ₹1,000 worth of rice to B while acting as agent for C, of which B has no knowledge or reasonable suspicion. C cannot compel B to take the rice without allowing set-off of A’s debt. Section 232 qualifies the principal’s right under s. 231. Current-law framing: establish undisclosed agency unknown to the third party; identify rights/obligations between agent and third party; apply those as a condition of the principal’s enforcement.

sections.heading: Contract with supposed principal
sections.body: One person contracts with another neither knowing nor having reasonable ground to suspect that the other is an agent.

sections.heading: Principal’s performance subject to equities
sections.body: The principal can obtain performance only subject to the rights and obligations between the agent and the other party.

sections.heading: Illustration
sections.body: Agent-seller who owes the buyer — principal cannot compel performance without allowing set-off of the agent’s debt.

provisions.title: Performance of contract with agent supposed to be principal

examples.title: Set-off of agent’s debt
examples.body: A owes B ₹500 and, as undisclosed agent for C, sells rice to B. C cannot compel B to take the rice without allowing set-off of A’s debt.

hypotheticals.question: Can an undisclosed principal always enforce free of the agent’s liabilities to the third party?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 232 subjects the principal’s enforcement to the rights and obligations between the agent and the other party.

distinctions.title: Performance subject to equities (s. 232) vs rights of parties on undisclosed agency (s. 231)
distinctions.left: Principal’s enforcement subject to agent–third party equities
distinctions.right: Principal may require performance; third party has same rights against principal as against agent

misconceptions.trap: An undisclosed principal always steps into the contract free of the agent’s personal position with the third party.
misconceptions.correction: Section 232 expressly subjects the principal’s performance right to existing rights and obligations between agent and third party.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 232 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Establish unknown/undisclosed agency. II. Identify rights and obligations between agent and third party. III. Condition principal’s enforcement on those equities. IV. Conclude.
